answer.location_description: Top-right corner of the image, roughly the top 5 rows and columns 15-22, well away from the centred nodule.
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units read this corner in opposite directions. The benign-leaning 'small compact nodule' units (0, 8, 25, also 5, 13, 14, 2) have extra positive weights there. The malignant-leaning 'large nodule / bright surround' units (10, 16, 12, 30, and the wide-field unit 19) have strong negative weights there. A bright patch in the top-right therefore raises the benign units and suppresses the malignant ones. Unit 0, for example, feeds layer-2 units u4, u8 and u15 with large negative weights, and those carry large positive output weights; it also feeds u0 and u7, which have negative output weights. Unit 9/10-type units feed u4 and u15 positively. The net effect is that the logit moves toward benign.
answer.evidence: Unit 10, rows 0-2, cols 15-21: about -40 to -52 (e.g. r0c21 = -52, r2c16 = -45, r2c20 = -45). Unit 16, same area: -39 to -56 (r0c20 = -56, r2c20 = -55, r1c16 = -47). Unit 19, rows 0-2, cols 12-23: a uniform block of -50 to -72. Unit 23: -40 to -60. Units 12 and 30: -30 to -38 there. The other three corners of these units carry only small or mixed weights, so the effect is specific to the top-right corner. Benign-leaning units are instead positive there: unit 0 r0c21 = 43, r3c20 = 44; unit 8 r0c21 = 45, r3c20 = 49; unit 25 r0c20 = 41, r3c19 = 40. Nothing else in the periphery shows this consistent cross-unit asymmetry. Anatomy around a centred nodule has no preferred corner, which suggests a spurious artifact.
answer.main_feature: Nodule size and extent around the centre. Units with a small bright centre and a dark ring push toward benign. Units with a negative centre and a bright surrounding ring (rows ~7-9 and 14-16), which respond to larger nodules, push toward malignant.
